memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'They must not leave any of it till morning or break any of its bones. When they celebrate the Passover, they must follow all the regulations. But if anyone who is ceremonially clean and not on a journey fails to celebrate the Passover, they must be cut off from their people for not presenting the Lord's offering at the appointed time. They will bear the consequences of their sin.'" - Num 9:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's grace in providing a second Passover was generous — but it was not an excuse for carelessness. The person who could have kept the Passover but simply chose not to bear a serious consequence. God's mercy toward the genuinely hindered was not meant to breed indifference in those who had no real reason to stay away.

This is an important balance. God is full of grace toward those held back by circumstances they cannot control. But He takes seriously the neglect of those who could draw near and simply do not bother. There is a difference between being unable and being unwilling.

We can sometimes twist God's grace into laziness, thinking, "God is merciful, so it does not matter if I neglect Him." But grace was never meant to make us casual about our relationship with God. The men in this chapter longed to come; the warning is for those who could come but choose not to.

Notice too the striking detail: "not break any of its bones." This small instruction about the Passover lamb finds a remarkable fulfilment. When Jesus, our Passover Lamb, died on the cross, the soldiers did not break His legs, and John points out that this fulfilled Scripture: "Not one of his bones will be broken" (John 19:36).

Even this tiny detail pointed to Christ. Let us treasure Him, our true Passover, and never grow casual about drawing near to the God who gave His Son for us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you ever twisted grace into an excuse for neglecting God?
- What is the difference between being unable and being unwilling to seek God?
- How does the unbroken lamb point you to Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for Your grace, but keep me from ever taking it lightly. Give me a heart that treasures drawing near to You through Christ, my Passover Lamb. Amen.
